en.intro: Hi, I'm NextStep. I'm here to help you look after your health, privately and at your own pace.
en.body:
Before we start, a few things:
• I'm a chatbot, not a doctor or nurse.
• Your chat is private. I won't ask your name and I never share your answers.
• We only keep total counts (like how many people visited a service) to improve NextStep.
• Type STOP anytime to end, or DELETE to erase your data.

Is that OK with you?
en.data:

• It is never sold or shared.
• Tip: you can turn off message previews in WhatsApp settings, and delete this chat anytime.

en.prompt: Ask me anything. Type your question (voice notes coming soon).
en.user_voice: Can I get HIV from kissing?
en.heard: I heard: "Can I get HIV from kissing?"
en.answer_kiss:
Good question. No. HIV is not passed on by kissing, hugging, or sharing cups or plates.

HIV can pass through sex without a condom, sharing needles, and from a mother to her baby. There are ways to prevent all of these.

Want to know how to stay protected?
en.protect:
Some ways to protect yourself:
• Use a condom every time.
• PrEP: a medicine that helps prevent HIV, for people who may be at higher risk. A health worker decides if it's right for you.
• Testing: know your status, and your partner's.

Want to find a free place to talk about PrEP?
en.unknown: Thanks for asking. I don't have a good answer to that yet, and I don't want to guess. A health worker at a youth-friendly service can help. Want me to find one?

en.intro: This is a private check: 6 quick questions, one at a time. There are no right or wrong answers. Your answers are only used to suggest a next step for you.
en.q1: In the last 6 months, have you had sex without a condom?
en.q2: Do you know your partner's HIV status?
en.q3: Have you had an HIV test in the last 6 months?
en.q4: Have you noticed any signs like unusual discharge, sores, or pain down there?
en.q5: Has anyone ever pressured or forced you to have sex? You don't have to answer.
en.q5_yes: Thank you for telling me. That is not okay, and it is not your fault. I'll share people who can support you at the end.
en.q6: Sometimes a partner gives money, gifts or support. Has a partner given you these and expected sex in return?
en.result_next:
Thank you for sharing. That took courage.

From your answers, an HIV test could help you know your status. You can do it privately with a self-test, or at a clinic.

You may also be able to get PrEP, a medicine that helps prevent HIV.

This is not a diagnosis. Only a test can tell you your status.
en.result_low:
Thank you for sharing. From your answers, your chance of HIV right now looks lower. That's good to know.

Testing regularly is still a smart habit. Want to see clinics near you?
en.result_sti: You mentioned some signs down there. A health worker can check this. It's common and it can be treated.
en.selftest:
An HIV self-test lets you test in private, with a mouth swab or a finger prick. Results take about 20 minutes.

If the result is reactive, you'll need a follow-up test at a clinic to confirm it.

Where to get one: [SELF-TEST DISTRIBUTION POINTS]
